P62E-COP-E-001.q: Which item is an explicit cost?
options: A payment to a materials supplier
P62E-COP-E-001.feedback: Explicit costs are direct monetary payments.

P62E-COP-E-002.q: Which item is an implicit cost?
options: A wage paid to an employee
The salary an owner gives up elsewhere
P62E-COP-E-002.feedback: Implicit costs are forgone alternatives of owner-supplied resources.

options: Revenue minus explicit and implicit costs
Revenue minus explicit and implicit costs
P62E-COP-E-004.feedback: Economic profit subtracts all opportunity costs.

options: All explicit and implicit costs are covered
P62E-COP-E-005.feedback: Zero economic profit includes normal profit.

P62E-COP-E-006.q: The short run is a period with:
options: Less than one year by definition
P62E-COP-E-006.feedback: The short run is defined by a fixed input.

P62E-COP-E-007.feedback: All inputs are adjustable in the long run.

P62E-COP-E-008.q: Which is usually variable in a short-run factory model?
P62E-COP-E-008.feedback: Labor can vary while capital is fixed.

options: Output added by the last worker
Additional output from one more input unit
P62E-COP-E-010.feedback: MP is the change in output.

options: Change in output divided by labor

P62E-COP-E-012.feedback: Diminishing MP begins with the first decline in MP.

P62E-COP-E-013.q: At zero short-run output, which cost remains?

options: Change in TFC divided by output
Change in TC divided by output
Change in TC divided by change in output
Change in revenue divided by output

P62E-COP-E-020.feedback: Fixed cost is spread over more units.

P62E-COP-E-022.q: If MC is below ATC, ATC:
P62E-COP-E-022.feedback: A marginal below the average pulls it down.

P62E-COP-E-023.feedback: MC crosses ATC at its minimum.

P62E-COP-E-024.feedback: Fixed cost affects AFC and ATC.

P62E-COP-E-025.feedback: A wage is a variable-input price.

P62E-COP-E-026.q: When MP rises at a constant wage, MC:

options: Exists only in the long run
The smallest output at minimum LRATC
P62E-COP-E-030.feedback: MES is the first minimum-LRATC output.

P62E-COP-E-031.q: Refer to the graph. At what output does AVC reach its minimum?
P62E-COP-E-031.feedback: The AVC curve bottoms out where MC crosses it, at Q=25.

P62E-COP-E-032.q: Refer to the graph. At what output does the average-cost curve reach its lowest point?
P62E-COP-E-032.feedback: The AC curve reaches its lowest point at Q=50.

P62E-COP-E-033.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 50, what is the vertical gap between AC and AVC?
P62E-COP-E-033.feedback: At Q=50, AC=$40 and AVC=$32, so the gap—and AFC—is $8.

P62E-COP-E-034.q: Refer to the graph. At what output does AVC reach its minimum value of $10?
P62E-COP-E-034.feedback: AVC bottoms out at Q=200 and $10.

P62E-COP-E-035.q: Refer to the graph. At what output is AC minimized?
P62E-COP-E-035.feedback: AC reaches its minimum at Q=400.

P62E-COP-E-036.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 400, what value of AVC is shown?
P62E-COP-E-036.feedback: The marked AVC value at Q=400 is $12.

P62E-COP-E-037.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 120, which labeled point lies on the total-cost curve?
P62E-COP-E-037.feedback: At Q=120, total cost is the upper curve at Point A ($1,200).

P62E-COP-E-038.q: Refer to the graph. Which labeled point marks $800 of variable cost at Q = 120?
P62E-COP-E-038.feedback: Point B marks TVC=$800 at Q=120.

P62E-COP-E-039.q: Refer to the graph. Which labeled point lies on the $400 fixed-cost line at Q = 120?
P62E-COP-E-039.feedback: Point C lies on the horizontal TFC line at $400.

P62E-COP-E-040.q: At about how many workers does total product reach its highest point on the graph?
P62E-COP-E-040.feedback: The TP curve peaks at about 10 workers.

P62E-COP-E-041.q: Refer to the graph. Approximately how much total product is produced at the peak of the TP curve?
P62E-COP-E-041.feedback: The peak occurs at roughly 150 units of total product.

P62E-COP-E-042.q: Refer to the graph. Which curve, MP or AP, reaches its peak at a lower labor input?
options: They peak at the same labor input
P62E-COP-E-042.feedback: The MP curve peaks before the AP curve.

P62E-COP-E-043.q: Refer to the graph. At about how many workers do MP and AP intersect?
P62E-COP-E-043.feedback: The curves cross at about seven workers.

P62E-COP-E-044.q: Refer to the graph. At what output does LRAC reach its minimum?
P62E-COP-E-044.feedback: The LRAC curve bottoms out at Q=60.

PMC-COP-E-001.q: An owner uses a building she could rent to another business for $2,000 per month. In economic-cost analysis, the forgone rent is:
PMC-COP-E-001.feedback: Using an owner-supplied resource sacrifices its next-best return, so the forgone rent is an implicit cost.

PMC-COP-E-002.q: Which cost is explicit for a small restaurant?
options: The owner’s forgone salary at another job
The interest the owner could have earned on invested savings
The rent the owner could earn from an owned building
The monthly payment to its food supplier
PMC-COP-E-002.feedback: An explicit cost is a direct monetary payment made by the firm.

options: Only payments that vary with output
Only costs paid in cash this month
Both explicit payments and implicit opportunity costs
Only costs recorded by an accountant
PMC-COP-E-003.feedback: Economic cost counts both recorded payments and the value of forgone alternatives.

PMC-COP-E-012.q: A firm has $150,000 in revenue and $110,000 in explicit costs. Its accounting profit is:
PMC-COP-E-012.feedback: Accounting profit equals revenue minus explicit costs.

options: Revenue minus explicit and implicit costs
PMC-COP-E-013.feedback: Economic profit subtracts all opportunity costs, including implicit costs.

PMC-COP-E-014.q: Normal profit is best understood as:
options: Revenue remaining after variable cost only
A payment excluded from economic cost
The return needed to keep owner-supplied resources in their current use
PMC-COP-E-014.feedback: Normal profit is part of implicit cost and represents the opportunity cost of entrepreneurial resources.

PMC-COP-E-015.q: If accounting profit is $60,000 and implicit costs are $25,000, economic profit is:
PMC-COP-E-015.feedback: Economic profit equals accounting profit minus implicit costs.

PMC-COP-E-016.q: A firm earning zero economic profit is:
options: Covering both explicit and implicit opportunity costs
PMC-COP-E-016.feedback: Zero economic profit includes normal compensation for owner resources.

PMC-COP-E-017.q: A firm can have positive accounting profit but negative economic profit when:
options: Implicit opportunity costs exceed accounting profit
Revenue exceeds all explicit and implicit costs
Normal profit is excluded from economic cost
PMC-COP-E-017.feedback: Accounting profit can look positive even though the owner would earn more in the next-best alternative.

PMC-COP-E-018.q: Positive economic profit means the firm’s revenue is:
options: Greater than explicit costs but below implicit costs
Exactly equal to total opportunity cost
Greater than all explicit and implicit costs
PMC-COP-E-018.feedback: Positive economic profit is the return above all opportunity costs.

PMC-COP-E-036.q: In the short run, total fixed cost generally:
options: Falls to zero whenever output is positive
Does not change when output changes
PMC-COP-E-036.feedback: Fixed cost is tied to inputs that cannot be adjusted in the short run.

PMC-COP-E-037.q: At zero output, total variable cost is typically:
PMC-COP-E-037.feedback: Variable cost is generated by producing output, so it is zero when output is zero in the standard cost model.

PMC-COP-E-038.q: A workshop has $150 of fixed cost and $90 of variable cost at its current output. Its total cost is:
PMC-COP-E-038.feedback: Total cost combines fixed and variable cost: $150 + $90 = $240.

PMC-COP-E-039.q: If total cost is $900 and total variable cost is $650, total fixed cost is:

PMC-COP-E-053.q: Which expression gives a firm’s fixed cost per unit of output?
options: Change in TC divided by change in Q
PMC-COP-E-053.feedback: Average fixed cost spreads total fixed cost across the units produced.

options: The change in total cost from producing additional output
Total cost per unit of output
PMC-COP-E-076.feedback: MC is the change in cost associated with a change in output.

PMC-COP-E-077.q: If output rises by 1 unit and total cost rises by $18, marginal cost of that unit is:
PMC-COP-E-077.feedback: With a one-unit output change, MC equals the increase in total cost.

PMC-COP-E-078.q: A pure increase in total fixed cost has what direct effect on marginal cost?
options: Raises MC by the full fixed-cost increase
PMC-COP-E-078.feedback: A constant addition to cost at every output does not change the cost of producing one more unit.

PMC-COP-E-079.q: With a constant wage, when marginal product of labor rises, marginal cost generally:
PMC-COP-E-079.feedback: More output from an additional worker lowers labor cost per extra unit.

PMC-COP-E-080.q: With a constant wage, diminishing marginal product eventually causes marginal cost to:
PMC-COP-E-080.feedback: When additional labor adds less output, each extra unit becomes more costly to produce.

PMC-COP-E-081.q: If TVC rises from $200 to $236 when output rises from 10 to 12 units, MC over that interval is:

PMC-COP-E-082.q: Marginal cost can be calculated from changes in TC or TVC because:
options: TVC is always equal to TC
TFC does not change with output
PMC-COP-E-082.feedback: Since fixed cost is unchanged, ΔTC = ΔTVC when output changes.

PMC-COP-E-083.q: If one additional worker costs $120 and adds 8 units of output, the labor-cost contribution to MC is:
PMC-COP-E-083.feedback: With a constant wage, $120/8 = $15 of labor cost per additional unit.

PMC-COP-E-094.q: ATC falls up to Q = 40 and rises beyond Q = 40. At Q = 40, which relationship should hold?
PMC-COP-E-094.feedback: Marginal cost intersects average total cost at ATC’s minimum.

PMC-COP-E-095.q: At the output where AVC reaches its minimum, which statement is correct?
PMC-COP-E-095.feedback: The marginal-cost curve passes through average variable cost at AVC’s minimum.

PMC-COP-E-096.q: A higher fixed license fee shifts which short-run average-cost curves upward?
PMC-COP-E-096.feedback: A fixed-cost increase raises fixed cost per unit and total cost per unit but leaves variable and marginal cost unchanged.

PMC-COP-E-097.q: A higher wage for production workers shifts which curves upward, other things equal?
PMC-COP-E-097.feedback: A production wage is a variable cost and affects the cost of additional output.

PMC-COP-E-104.q: A sunk cost is a cost that:
options: Exists only when economic profit is negative
Has already been incurred and cannot be recovered
Can always be avoided by shutting down today
PMC-COP-E-104.feedback: A sunk cost is unrecoverable and should not be changed by the current decision.

PMC-COP-E-105.q: An avoidable cost is a cost that:
options: Can be eliminated by choosing a particular alternative
Has already been paid and cannot be recovered
Must be fixed in every time period
PMC-COP-E-105.feedback: Avoidable costs differ across the alternatives being considered.

PMC-COP-E-106.q: A nonrefundable $2,000 design fee was paid last month. For today’s continue-or-cancel decision, the fee is:
PMC-COP-E-106.feedback: The payment cannot be recovered regardless of the current choice.

PMC-COP-E-107.q: A monthly service contract can be canceled before next month with no penalty. Next month’s payment is:
PMC-COP-E-107.feedback: A future cost that disappears under one option is relevant to the decision.

PMC-COP-E-123.q: Long-run average cost shows the lowest attainable average cost when:
options: At least one input is fixed
PMC-COP-E-123.feedback: The long run allows the firm to choose among plant sizes and adjust all inputs.

PMC-COP-E-124.q: LRAC falls from $28 per unit to $21 per unit as a firm expands its long-run output. This pattern indicates:
options: Diminishing marginal product from a fixed plant
PMC-COP-E-124.feedback: Falling long-run average cost as scale expands indicates economies of scale.

PMC-COP-E-125.q: A very large firm becomes harder to coordinate, and its long-run cost per unit rises as it expands further. This is:
options: A fall in total product caused by one fixed input
PMC-COP-E-125.feedback: Rising unit cost at greater scale is diseconomies of scale; coordination problems are a common source.

PMC-COP-E-126.q: The LRAC curve is often described as an envelope because it:
options: Adds all short-run fixed costs together
Shows the highest ATC at every output
Is identical to one short-run ATC curve
Traces the lowest attainable ATC across available plant sizes
PMC-COP-E-126.feedback: In the long run, the firm can choose the least-cost plant for each output level.

PMC-COP-E-127.q: Which is a common source of economies of scale?
options: A fall in marginal product caused by one fixed input
Greater specialization as the firm expands
A fixed input becoming more crowded
PMC-COP-E-127.feedback: Larger scale can support specialization of labor and capital that lowers average cost.

PMC-COP-E-128.q: Which is a common source of diseconomies of scale?
options: Coordination and communication problems in a very large organization
Spreading fixed cost over more units only
PMC-COP-E-128.feedback: Large scale can raise organizational and coordination costs per unit.

PMC-COP-E-129.q: Why can a firm choose a different plant size in long-run cost analysis?
options: All inputs are variable in the long run
Plant size is always variable in the short run
Fixed cost is zero at every output
Marginal cost determines plant size automatically
PMC-COP-E-129.feedback: The long run is defined by enough time to adjust all inputs, including plant capacity.

options: Largest output the firm can physically produce
Output where total cost is lowest
First output where marginal product is positive
Smallest output at which minimum LRAC is attained
PMC-COP-E-150.feedback: MES marks the first output level that reaches the minimum long-run average cost.

PMC-COP-E-151.q: A flat LRAC over a range of output is associated with:
options: Diseconomies of scale throughout the range
Economies of scale throughout the range
PMC-COP-E-151.feedback: A flat long-run average cost means proportional expansion does not change cost per unit.

PMC-COP-E-152.q: If LRAC first reaches its minimum at 5,000 units and remains flat until 8,000, MES is:
PMC-COP-E-152.feedback: MES is the smallest output that attains the minimum LRAC.

PMC-COP-E-153.q: With constant returns to scale, doubling all inputs tends to:
options: Increase output by less than double
PMC-COP-E-153.feedback: Constant returns means output changes in the same proportion as all inputs.

P62E-COP-M-001.q: Maya runs Northstar Bakery. Revenue is $186,000, explicit cost $118,000, forgone salary $42,000, and forgone capital income $12,000. Economic profit?

P62E-COP-M-002.q: Ironwood Furniture earns $242,000 and pays $151,000 in recorded expenses. Accounting profit?

P62E-COP-M-004.q: Cedar Trail Bikes earns $311,000 and pays $203,000 in recorded expenses. Accounting profit?

P62E-COP-M-006.q: Riverbend Textiles earns $274,000 and pays $176,000 in recorded expenses. Accounting profit?

P62E-COP-M-007.q: Evan runs Juniper Foods. Revenue is $205,000, explicit cost $132,000, forgone salary $44,000, and forgone capital income $11,000. Economic profit?

P62E-COP-M-008.q: Summit Glassworks earns $356,000 and pays $229,000 in recorded expenses. Accounting profit?

P62E-COP-M-009.q: Owen runs Maple Street Media. Revenue is $149,000, explicit cost $89,000, forgone salary $35,000, and forgone capital income $8,000. Economic profit?

P62E-COP-M-010.q: Granite Toolworks earns $298,000 and pays $188,000 in recorded expenses. Accounting profit?

P62E-COP-M-011.q: At Northstar Bakery, output rises from 8 to 20 when worker 2 is added. MP?

P62E-COP-M-012.q: Ironwood Furniture has TFC $300, employs 3 workers at $135, and produces 29 units. TC?
P62E-COP-M-012.feedback: Add TFC and the wage bill.

P62E-COP-M-013.q: At Harbor Roasters, output rises from 36 to 47 when worker 4 is added. MP?

P62E-COP-M-014.q: Cedar Trail Bikes has TFC $420, employs 5 workers at $150, and produces 54 units. TC?
P62E-COP-M-014.feedback: Add TFC and the wage bill.

P62E-COP-M-015.q: At Blue Peak Printing, output rises from 53 to 61 when worker 6 is added. MP?

P62E-COP-M-016.q: Riverbend Textiles has TFC $360, employs 2 workers at $140, and produces 25 units. TC?
P62E-COP-M-016.feedback: Add TFC and the wage bill.

P62E-COP-M-017.q: At Juniper Foods, output rises from 19 to 32 when worker 3 is added. MP?

P62E-COP-M-018.q: Summit Glassworks has TFC $480, employs 4 workers at $160, and produces 57 units. TC?
P62E-COP-M-018.feedback: Add TFC and the wage bill.

P62E-COP-M-019.q: At Maple Street Media, output rises from 37 to 47 when worker 5 is added. MP?

P62E-COP-M-020.q: Granite Toolworks has TFC $390, employs 6 workers at $145, and produces 72 units. TC?
P62E-COP-M-020.feedback: Add TFC and the wage bill.

P62E-COP-M-021.q: On the TP graph, after MP begins to diminish, TP can:
P62E-COP-M-021.feedback: Positive but declining MP still raises TP.

P62E-COP-M-022.q: The first downward move of MP marks:
P62E-COP-M-022.feedback: Diminishing MP starts when MP first falls.

P62E-COP-M-023.q: If MP is above AP, AP is:
P62E-COP-M-023.feedback: A marginal above the average raises it.

P62E-COP-M-024.q: The vertical gap between TC and TVC is:

P62E-COP-M-026.feedback: MC crosses AVC at its minimum.

P62E-COP-M-027.q: A fixed-cost increase leaves AVC unchanged because:
options: Fixed cost is not part of TVC
P62E-COP-M-027.feedback: A pure fixed-cost change does not affect AVC.

P62E-COP-M-028.q: A higher wage shifts MC upward because:
options: Added output now requires more variable spending
P62E-COP-M-028.feedback: The wage is a variable-input cost.

options: More output comes from the same inputs

P62E-COP-M-030.feedback: Falling LRATC is economies of scale.

P62E-COP-M-031.q: Refer to the graph. At the MC–AVC intersection at Q = 25, what is marginal cost?
P62E-COP-M-031.feedback: The MC and AVC curves meet at Q=25 and cost $30.

P62E-COP-M-032.q: Refer to the graph. At the MC–AC intersection at Q = 50, what is marginal cost?
P62E-COP-M-032.feedback: MC crosses AC at Q=50 and $40.

P62E-COP-M-033.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 50, what total fixed cost is implied by the gap between AC and AVC?

P62E-COP-M-034.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 200, what value does the MC–AVC intersection show?
P62E-COP-M-034.feedback: MC equals AVC at the AVC minimum, $10 at Q=200.

P62E-COP-M-035.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 400, what value does the MC–AC intersection show?
P62E-COP-M-035.feedback: MC and AC meet at $20 when Q=400.

P62E-COP-M-036.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 400, what does the gap between AC and AVC imply about AFC?
P62E-COP-M-036.feedback: At Q=400, AC=$20 and AVC=$12, so AFC=$8.

P62E-COP-M-037.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 120, what is the vertical distance between Points A and B?
P62E-COP-M-037.feedback: The gap is $1,200−$800=$400, equal to TFC.

P62E-COP-M-038.q: Refer to the graph. Using Point A at Q = 120, what is average total cost?

P62E-COP-M-039.q: Refer to the graph. Using Point B at Q = 120, approximately what is average variable cost?

P62E-COP-M-040.q: Refer to the graph. At the labor input where total product reaches its maximum, what is marginal product?
P62E-COP-M-040.feedback: At the peak of TP, the slope of TP—and therefore MP—is zero.

P62E-COP-M-041.q: For labor inputs to the right of the total-product maximum, what sign does marginal product have?
P62E-COP-M-041.feedback: A downward-sloping TP curve means each added worker reduces total output, so MP is negative.

P62E-COP-M-042.q: At about 5 workers, how is MP positioned relative to AP on the graph?
options: MP is negative while AP is positive
P62E-COP-M-042.feedback: Near five workers, the red MP curve lies above the green AP curve.

P62E-COP-M-043.q: At about 9 workers, which comparison matches the graph?
options: MP is above AP and remains positive
MP equals AP at that labor input
MP is negative while AP remains at zero
MP is below AP but still positive
P62E-COP-M-043.feedback: Near nine workers, MP is positive but lies below AP.

P62E-COP-M-044.q: Refer to the graph. Near 10 workers, what happens to marginal product?
options: MP equals the peak of AP
MP becomes equal to total product
P62E-COP-M-044.feedback: The MP curve crosses the horizontal axis at about ten workers.

P62E-COP-M-045.q: Approximately what LRAC does the graph show at Q=30?
P62E-COP-M-045.feedback: At Q=30, the curve is near the $20 gridline.

P62E-COP-M-046.q: Refer to the graph. What LRAC is shown at Q = 90?
P62E-COP-M-046.feedback: At Q=90, the curve is again near $20.

PMC-COP-M-004.q: A photographer quits a $48,000 salaried job to operate a studio she owns. She makes no wage payment to herself. The $48,000 is best treated as:
options: An implicit cost of operating the studio
A sunk cost from the former job
PMC-COP-M-004.feedback: The salary sacrificed by using the owner’s labor in the business is an opportunity cost.

PMC-COP-M-005.q: A business uses $100,000 of the owner’s savings that could earn 5% elsewhere. Which amount belongs in economic cost because of that choice?
PMC-COP-M-005.feedback: The relevant implicit cost is the return sacrificed on the owner’s capital: 5% of $100,000.

PMC-COP-M-006.q: A firm rents one warehouse for $30,000 and uses a second warehouse owned by the proprietor that could rent for $24,000. Which statement is correct?
options: Only the $24,000 belongs in economic cost
The $30,000 is explicit and the $24,000 is implicit
PMC-COP-M-006.feedback: The rental payment is explicit; forgone rent on owner-owned property is an implicit opportunity cost.

PMC-COP-M-007.q: A contractor owns a truck that could be leased to another firm for $9,000 a year. If the truck is used in the contractor’s own business, the $9,000 is:
options: A fixed accounting payment to the owner
Irrelevant because no cash changes hands
Part of the business’s economic cost
An accounting expense only if the truck is sold
PMC-COP-M-007.feedback: The forgone lease income is the opportunity cost of using the truck internally.

PMC-COP-M-008.q: Recorded expenses are $70,000. The owner also gives up a $40,000 salary and $5,000 of interest. Total economic cost is:
PMC-COP-M-008.feedback: Economic cost equals explicit cost plus all implicit opportunity costs: $70,000 + $40,000 + $5,000.

PMC-COP-M-040.q: A firm’s TFC is $120. At an output of 8 units, TVC is $280. TC is:

PMC-COP-M-041.q: A cost schedule shows TC of $510 at 5 units and TFC of $150. TVC at 5 units is:

PMC-COP-M-042.q: A firm’s TC is $200 at zero output and $470 at 6 units. What is TFC?
PMC-COP-M-042.feedback: At zero output, TVC is zero, so TC equals TFC.

PMC-COP-M-054.q: TFC is $240 and output is 12 units. AFC is:

PMC-COP-M-055.q: TVC is $360 at 18 units of output. AVC is:

PMC-COP-M-056.q: TC is $600 at 20 units. ATC is:

PMC-COP-M-057.q: At 10 units, AFC is $8 and AVC is $22. ATC is:

PMC-COP-M-058.q: A firm’s TFC is unchanged while output doubles. What happens to AFC?
PMC-COP-M-058.feedback: AFC = TFC/Q, so doubling Q with the same TFC halves AFC.

PMC-COP-M-059.q: At 25 units, ATC is $18 and AFC is $4. AVC is:

PMC-COP-M-060.q: A firm has TFC = $100, TVC = $300, and Q = 20. Which pair is correct?

PMC-COP-M-084.q: Total cost rises from $540 to $600 as output rises from 20 to 24 units. Marginal cost over the interval is:

PMC-COP-M-085.q: A worker costs $180 per shift. The worker’s marginal product falls from 12 units to 9 units as employment expands. Holding the wage constant, the implied labor cost per marginal unit changes from:
PMC-COP-M-085.feedback: W/MP rises from 180/12 = 15 to 180/9 = 20 as marginal product falls.

PMC-COP-M-086.q: A $500 monthly license fee is imposed regardless of output. Which statement about MC is correct?
options: MC rises by $500 for every unit
MC is unchanged because the fee does not vary with output
PMC-COP-M-086.feedback: A fixed fee shifts fixed and average total cost, not the incremental cost of output.

PMC-COP-M-087.q: A technology change lets each additional worker produce more output at the same wage. What happens to marginal cost, other things equal?
PMC-COP-M-087.feedback: Higher marginal product means the same labor expense creates more additional output.

PMC-COP-M-088.q: TVC is $300 at 15 units and $390 at 20 units. What is MC between these outputs?

PMC-COP-M-098.q: MC is below AVC but rising. What must AVC be doing at that output?
PMC-COP-M-098.feedback: A marginal below the average pulls the average downward even if the marginal itself is rising.

PMC-COP-M-099.q: MC is above ATC. What must be happening to ATC?
PMC-COP-M-099.feedback: A marginal above the average pulls the average upward.

PMC-COP-M-100.q: A technology improvement reduces the variable input needed at every output. Which short-run curves should generally shift downward?
PMC-COP-M-100.feedback: Lower variable resource requirements reduce variable cost per unit and marginal cost.

PMC-COP-M-101.q: At a given output, ATC is $30 and AVC is $24. The vertical gap between those curves is:

PMC-COP-M-108.q: A theater paid $5,000 for an advertising campaign that cannot be refunded. It is deciding whether to hold an event tomorrow. How should the $5,000 enter the decision?
options: It should determine the ticket price
It should be ignored because it is sunk
It should be charged again to tomorrow’s event
It should be treated as marginal cost of each ticket
PMC-COP-M-108.feedback: The advertising payment is unrecoverable and identical under either current choice.

PMC-COP-M-109.q: A firm can cancel a future equipment rental and save $3,000 if it stops a project. The $3,000 is:
options: An avoidable cost relevant to the stop-or-continue choice
A sunk cost because equipment is fixed
An implicit cost with no monetary payment
Irrelevant because it is a fixed monthly amount
PMC-COP-M-109.feedback: Future fixed commitments can be avoidable if the decision eliminates them.

PMC-COP-M-110.q: A company spent $40,000 developing software that now has no resale value. A new update would cost $8,000 and generate an expected $11,000 benefit. Ignoring other effects, what should the firm do?
options: Reject the update because total spending would become $48,000
Reject the update because sunk costs must be recovered first
Buy the update only if the original $40,000 is refunded
Buy the update because the $40,000 is sunk and the incremental benefit exceeds the incremental cost
PMC-COP-M-110.feedback: The current decision compares the $11,000 additional benefit with the $8,000 additional cost.

PMC-COP-M-111.q: A store’s current lease payment is nonrefundable, but the lease ends this month. The owner is deciding whether to renew for another year. Which cost is relevant?
options: Neither payment because rent is fixed
PMC-COP-M-111.feedback: The current payment is sunk; the future renewal is avoidable and differs across options.

PMC-COP-M-112.q: A firm owns a specialized machine with no resale value. Its original purchase price is irrelevant to whether to use it for a new order because the purchase price is:
PMC-COP-M-112.feedback: An unrecoverable past expenditure does not change across the current alternatives.

PMC-COP-M-130.q: Assume input prices are unchanged. A distribution network uses 40% more labor, buildings, and equipment but can handle 60% more shipments. This pattern is consistent with:
PMC-COP-M-130.feedback: With unchanged input prices, total input cost rises in proportion to inputs while output rises by a larger percentage, so long-run average cost falls—consistent with economies of scale.

PMC-COP-M-131.q: Assume input prices are unchanged. A company expands every input by 25%, but output increases by only 10%. Which scale result does this suggest?
PMC-COP-M-131.feedback: With unchanged input prices, total input cost rises in proportion to inputs while output rises by a smaller percentage, so long-run average cost rises—consistent with diseconomies of scale.

PMC-COP-M-132.q: Plant A has ATC $18 at 500 units and Plant B has ATC $15 at 500 units. If both plants are feasible in the long run, LRAC at 500 units cannot exceed:
PMC-COP-M-132.feedback: The firm can choose the lower-cost plant, so the long-run attainable average cost is at most $15.

PMC-COP-M-133.q: LRAC falls from $24 to $18 as output rises from 2,000 to 4,000 units. The firm is operating in a range of:
PMC-COP-M-133.feedback: Average cost is falling as the scale of production expands.

PMC-COP-M-134.q: LRAC rises from $14 to $17 as output rises from 8,000 to 10,000 units. The firm is experiencing:
PMC-COP-M-134.feedback: Rising long-run average cost with greater scale indicates diseconomies of scale.

PMC-COP-M-135.q: Which statement best distinguishes LRAC from a single SRATC curve?
options: LRAC is total cost rather than average cost
LRAC reflects the least-cost plant choice at each output; a SRATC holds plant size fixed
LRAC holds all inputs fixed while SRATC varies all inputs
PMC-COP-M-135.feedback: Long-run cost allows plant adjustment; a particular short-run curve corresponds to a given plant.

PMC-COP-M-136.q: A larger factory permits dedicated machinery and specialized teams that reduce unit cost. This is an example of:
options: Diminishing marginal product from a fixed plant
PMC-COP-M-136.feedback: Specialization and indivisible technologies can lower LRAC as scale expands.

PMC-COP-M-154.feedback: The minimum LRAC is $12, first reached at 4,000 units.

PMC-COP-M-155.q: A firm increases all inputs by 25% and output also rises by 25%. This is consistent with:
options: Diminishing marginal product caused by fixed capital
PMC-COP-M-155.feedback: Output changes in the same proportion as all inputs.

PMC-COP-M-156.q: A firm’s LRAC reaches a flat minimum from 10,000 to 14,000 units. Which output is the minimum efficient scale?
PMC-COP-M-156.feedback: MES is the first output on the minimum-cost range.

PMC-COP-M-157.q: LRAC is $16 at both 20,000 and 30,000 units, and the curve is flat between them. Over that range the firm experiences:
PMC-COP-M-157.feedback: An unchanged long-run cost per unit over a range is consistent with constant returns to scale.

PMC-COP-M-158.q: Why is the largest output on a flat minimum-LRAC segment not the MES?
options: MES is always the midpoint of the flat segment
MES is the output with highest total cost
MES requires LRAC to begin rising
MES is defined as the smallest output that attains minimum LRAC
PMC-COP-M-158.feedback: Larger outputs may also be efficient, but MES identifies the minimum scale needed to achieve the lowest unit cost.

P62E-COP-H-001.q: Northstar Bakery pays each worker $120. Worker 3 raises output from 20 to 34. Which pair is correct?
options: MP=14 units and MC=$8.57 per unit
P62E-COP-H-001.feedback: MP is the output change; with a constant wage, MC is wage divided by MP.

P62E-COP-H-002.q: At Ironwood Furniture, Q=41, TFC=$300, and 4 workers each cost $135. Which cost identity is correct?
P62E-COP-H-002.feedback: Divide each total by output and verify ATC=AFC+AVC.

P62E-COP-H-003.q: Harbor Roasters has output schedule 0:0, 1:10, 2:23, 3:36, 4:47, 5:56, 6:63, 7:68, 8:71. With all else fixed, diminishing marginal product first appears when which worker is added?
P62E-COP-H-003.feedback: Find the first worker whose marginal product is below the previous worker’s marginal product.

P62E-COP-H-004.q: Cedar Trail Bikes pays each worker $150. Worker 6 raises output from 54 to 60. Which pair is correct?
options: MP=6 units and MC=$25 per unit
P62E-COP-H-004.feedback: MP is the output change; with a constant wage, MC is wage divided by MP.

P62E-COP-H-005.q: At Blue Peak Printing, Q=31, TFC=$210, and 3 workers each cost $110. Which cost identity is correct?
P62E-COP-H-005.feedback: Divide each total by output and verify ATC=AFC+AVC.

P62E-COP-H-006.q: Riverbend Textiles has output schedule 0:0, 1:11, 2:25, 3:40, 4:53, 5:64, 6:73, 7:80, 8:85. With all else fixed, diminishing marginal product first appears when which worker is added?
P62E-COP-H-006.feedback: Find the first worker whose marginal product is below the previous worker’s marginal product.

P62E-COP-H-007.q: Juniper Foods pays each worker $125. Worker 5 raises output from 44 to 54. Which pair is correct?
options: MP=10 units and MC=$12.50 per unit
P62E-COP-H-007.feedback: MP is the output change; with a constant wage, MC is wage divided by MP.

P62E-COP-H-008.q: At Summit Glassworks, Q=79, TFC=$480, and 6 workers each cost $160. Which cost identity is correct?
P62E-COP-H-008.feedback: Divide each total by output and verify ATC=AFC+AVC.

P62E-COP-H-009.q: Maple Street Media has output schedule 0:0, 1:6, 2:15, 3:26, 4:37, 5:47, 6:55, 7:61, 8:65. With all else fixed, diminishing marginal product first appears when which worker is added?
P62E-COP-H-009.feedback: Find the first worker whose marginal product is below the previous worker’s marginal product.

P62E-COP-H-010.q: Granite Toolworks pays each worker $145. Worker 4 raises output from 39 to 52. Which pair is correct?
options: MP=13 units and MC=$11.15 per unit
P62E-COP-H-010.feedback: MP is the output change; with a constant wage, MC is wage divided by MP.

P62E-COP-H-011.q: At Lakeside Ceramics, Q=58, TFC=$225, and 5 workers each cost $115. Which cost identity is correct?
P62E-COP-H-011.feedback: Divide each total by output and verify ATC=AFC+AVC.

P62E-COP-H-012.q: Prairie Solar has output schedule 0:0, 1:13, 2:29, 3:46, 4:61, 5:74, 6:85, 7:94, 8:101. With all else fixed, diminishing marginal product first appears when which worker is added?
P62E-COP-H-012.feedback: Find the first worker whose marginal product is below the previous worker’s marginal product.

P62E-COP-H-013.q: On this graph, MC is rising but remains below ATC. What must be happening to ATC?
P62E-COP-H-013.feedback: A rising marginal can still pull the average down while it remains below that average.

P62E-COP-H-014.q: A firm receives a property-tax increase that does not depend on output. Which immediate short-run curve change is correct?
options: AVC and MC shift upward together
ATC shifts upward while AVC is unchanged
P62E-COP-H-014.feedback: A property tax is fixed with respect to output.

P62E-COP-H-015.q: The wage paid to every production worker rises. Which curve combination shifts upward?
P62E-COP-H-015.feedback: The wage changes variable and marginal costs.

P62E-COP-H-016.q: A process improvement raises output from every labor level. With input prices unchanged, the most defensible cost prediction is:
options: AFC rises and MC is unchanged
MC and ATC shift downward over the affected output range
All costs rise because output rises
P62E-COP-H-016.feedback: More output from the same inputs reduces marginal and average cost.

P62E-COP-H-017.q: Which statement about the two crossings in this cost family is correct?
options: MC crosses both at the same quantity by definition
MC crosses each average at its maximum
MC crosses AVC and ATC at each curve’s own minimum
AFC crosses both averages at their minima
P62E-COP-H-017.feedback: The marginal crosses each average at that average’s minimum.

P62E-COP-H-018.q: The narrowing vertical distance between ATC and AVC is evidence that:
P62E-COP-H-018.feedback: The gap equals AFC, which declines as output rises.

P62E-COP-H-019.q: On the total-cost graph, TC and TVC remain vertically parallel because:
P62E-COP-H-019.feedback: TC=TVC+TFC, so a constant TFC is the vertical gap.

P62E-COP-H-020.q: Where LRATC is flat over an output interval, the firm experiences:
P62E-COP-H-020.feedback: A flat LRATC indicates unchanged cost per unit as all inputs and output expand proportionally.

P62E-COP-H-021.q: The first output at which the flat minimum begins is:
P62E-COP-H-021.feedback: MES is the smallest output attaining minimum LRATC.

options: The average of all SRATC curves
The highest fixed cost at each output
The lowest attainable ATC among available plant sizes at each output
P62E-COP-H-022.feedback: In the long run the firm can choose the least-cost plant for each output.

P62E-COP-H-023.q: A firm’s accounting profit is $90,000 and its owner forgoes a $55,000 salary plus $15,000 of interest. Economic profit is:
P62E-COP-H-023.feedback: Subtract both implicit costs from accounting profit.

P62E-COP-H-024.q: A firm has zero economic profit and positive accounting profit. The best interpretation is:
options: The firm cannot pay its bills
Revenue covers explicit costs and the owner’s opportunity costs
P62E-COP-H-024.feedback: Zero economic profit includes normal compensation for owner resources.

P62E-COP-H-025.q: A machine lease can be canceled next month without penalty, but the current month’s payment is already made. For a decision next month, the lease is:
P62E-COP-H-025.feedback: Future fixed commitments can be avoidable even when current payments are sunk.

P62E-COP-H-026.q: Assume input prices are unchanged. A firm doubles every input and output rises by only 70%. This is evidence of:
P62E-COP-H-026.feedback: With unchanged input prices, total input cost rises in proportion to inputs while output rises by a smaller percentage, so long-run average cost rises—consistent with diseconomies of scale.

P62E-COP-H-027.q: Assume input prices are unchanged. A firm doubles every input and output more than doubles. LRATC should generally:
P62E-COP-H-027.feedback: With unchanged input prices, output rises more than proportionally to total input cost, so long-run average cost falls.

P62E-COP-H-028.q: Which change can lower MC without changing TFC?
options: A higher marginal product of labor
P62E-COP-H-028.feedback: Higher MP means fewer variable-input dollars per extra unit.

P62E-COP-H-029.q: A firm’s MC is below AVC but above ATC. This combination is:
P62E-COP-H-029.feedback: Since ATC=AVC+AFC, ATC is above AVC; MC cannot be below AVC and above ATC simultaneously.

P62E-COP-H-030.q: A firm chooses the output with the lowest total cost. Why is that rule defective?
options: Different output levels cannot be compared using total cost alone
P62E-COP-H-030.feedback: The level of total cost alone does not identify the best output. An output decision requires comparing the additional revenue and additional cost associated with changing quantity.

P62E-COP-H-031.q: Refer to the graph. Around Q = 35, as output rises slightly, which pattern is consistent with the cost curves?
P62E-COP-H-031.feedback: Around Q=35, MC lies above AVC but below AC, so it pulls AVC up and AC down.

P62E-COP-H-032.q: Refer to the graph. Just to the right of Q = 50, what happens to both average-cost curves as output increases?
P62E-COP-H-032.feedback: Beyond Q=50, MC lies above both averages, so both are pulled upward.

P62E-COP-H-033.q: Refer to the graph. To the left of Q = 25, which movement of the average-cost curves is consistent with the graph?
options: Both AC and AVC are falling
Both AC and AVC are rising together
AC rises while AVC continues falling
AC is flat while AVC continues rising
P62E-COP-H-033.feedback: Before the AVC minimum, MC is below the average curves, pulling them downward.

P62E-COP-H-034.q: Refer to the graph. Around Q = 300, what happens to AVC and AC as output rises?
P62E-COP-H-034.feedback: Between the two minima, MC is above AVC but below AC.

P62E-COP-H-035.q: Refer to the graph. Immediately to the right of the AC minimum near Q = 400, what happens to AC?
options: MC is below AC, so AC rises
MC is above AVC, so AVC falls
MC equals AFC, so AC is flat
MC is above AC, so AC rises
P62E-COP-H-035.feedback: Past the AC minimum, MC lies above AC and pulls it upward.

P62E-COP-H-036.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 400, what total fixed cost is implied by the marked values?
P62E-COP-H-036.feedback: AFC is $20−$12=$8; multiplying by 400 units gives TFC=$3,200.

P62E-COP-H-037.q: Refer to the graph. At Q = 120, approximately what is average fixed cost at Point C?

P62E-COP-H-038.q: The graph shows the upper and middle curves staying a constant vertical distance apart. Which fact explains that pattern?
options: Both curves are measures of fixed cost
Variable cost is constant at every output
Their difference is the constant TFC
P62E-COP-H-038.feedback: TC−TVC=TFC, and TFC is constant in the short run.

P62E-COP-H-039.q: Refer to the graph. At zero output, what explains the vertical gap between the total-cost and variable-cost curves?
P62E-COP-H-039.feedback: Fixed cost is incurred even when output is zero.

P62E-COP-H-040.q: Refer to the graph. Between about 6 and 9 workers, which description of marginal product fits the total-product curve?
options: MP is positive and increasing throughout
P62E-COP-H-040.feedback: TP still rises, so MP is positive; the flattening slope shows MP is decreasing.

P62E-COP-H-041.q: Refer to the graph. After total product reaches its maximum, which combination of total product and marginal product is consistent with the curve?
options: TP rises and MP is negative
TP falls and MP is positive
TP is constant and MP is positive
TP falls and MP is negative
P62E-COP-H-041.feedback: The falling TP curve after its peak means marginal product is negative.

P62E-COP-H-042.q: Refer to the graph. At the marked labor input where MP lies above AP, what happens to AP when another worker is added?
P62E-COP-H-042.feedback: A marginal value above the average pulls the average upward.

P62E-COP-H-043.q: Refer to the graph. At the marked labor input where MP is below AP but still positive, what happens to TP and AP as another worker is added?
options: TP is constant while AP rises
P62E-COP-H-043.feedback: Positive MP raises TP, but MP below AP pulls AP downward.

P62E-COP-H-044.q: At the point where the MP and AP curves intersect, what is true of average product?
options: MP is at its own maximum
P62E-COP-H-044.feedback: An average is maximized where the marginal value crosses it from above.

P62E-COP-H-045.q: Refer to the graph. If output expands from about 30 toward 60 units, what happens to LRAC?
options: LRAC rises, indicating diseconomies of scale
LRAC falls, indicating economies of scale
LRAC falls, indicating diseconomies of scale
P62E-COP-H-045.feedback: The left side of the U-shaped LRAC slopes downward toward its minimum.

P62E-COP-H-046.q: If a firm expands output from about 60 toward 90 units, what happens to LRAC?
options: LRAC falls, indicating economies of scale
LRAC stays at the minimum of about $12
LRAC rises, indicating diseconomies of scale
LRAC rises, indicating economies of scale
P62E-COP-H-046.feedback: To the right of the minimum, LRAC rises as scale expands.

PMC-COP-H-009.q: Two otherwise identical businesses each pay $80,000 in recorded expenses. Owner A gives up a $50,000 salary; Owner B gives up a $35,000 salary and $20,000 of investment income. Which has the higher economic cost?
options: They have the same economic cost
It cannot be determined without revenue
PMC-COP-H-009.feedback: A has $130,000 of economic cost; B has $135,000 because both forgone salary and forgone investment income count.

PMC-COP-H-019.q: A proprietor reports $95,000 of accounting profit. She gives up a $65,000 salary and $18,000 of interest by operating the business. What is her economic profit?
PMC-COP-H-019.feedback: Subtract both implicit costs from accounting profit: $95,000 − $65,000 − $18,000.

PMC-COP-H-020.q: Firm A earns $70,000 accounting profit and has $20,000 implicit cost. Firm B earns $90,000 accounting profit and has $50,000 implicit cost. Which has the larger economic profit?
PMC-COP-H-020.feedback: Firm A earns $50,000 economic profit; Firm B earns $40,000.

PMC-COP-H-021.q: An owner could earn $75,000 elsewhere and could earn $10,000 interest on invested capital. The firm’s accounting profit is $85,000. Which statement is correct?
options: The firm earns zero economic profit
PMC-COP-H-021.feedback: The $85,000 accounting profit exactly covers the $85,000 of implicit opportunity costs.

PMC-COP-H-022.q: A firm’s revenue rises by $20,000 while explicit costs rise by $8,000 and implicit costs rise by $5,000. Compared with before, economic profit changes by:
PMC-COP-H-022.feedback: Economic profit changes by the revenue change minus both cost changes: $20,000 − $8,000 − $5,000.

PMC-COP-H-061.q: At Q = 40, ATC is $25 and AFC is $5. If TFC is unchanged, what is TVC at this output?

PMC-COP-H-062.q: AFC falls from $12 to $8 while TFC remains $240. Output must have changed from:
PMC-COP-H-062.feedback: Q = TFC/AFC, so output rises from 240/12 = 20 to 240/8 = 30.

PMC-COP-H-063.q: At Q = 50, TC is $1,400 and TFC is $400. Which average-cost values are correct?

PMC-COP-H-064.q: A firm’s AVC is $16 at 30 units and its AFC is $6. If output rises and AFC falls to $4 while AVC stays $16, ATC becomes:

PMC-COP-H-113.q: A firm has already paid a nonrefundable $6,000 permit fee. Completing a project requires $14,000 more and will generate $17,000 in additional revenue. What is the correct decision logic?
options: Complete the project because the relevant incremental gain is $3,000
Cancel because the permit fee must be recovered
PMC-COP-H-113.feedback: The sunk permit is irrelevant; compare $17,000 additional revenue with $14,000 avoidable completion cost.

PMC-COP-H-114.q: A plant pays $10,000 per month on a contract. If it closes now, $7,000 can be canceled but $3,000 must still be paid. For the close-or-operate choice, how much of the monthly contract is avoidable?
PMC-COP-H-114.feedback: Only the portion that disappears when the plant closes is avoidable.

PMC-COP-H-115.q: A publisher spent $25,000 editing a book. It can print the book for an additional $12,000 and expects $15,000 in additional sales. Which statement is correct?
options: The editing cost should be allocated to each future copy before deciding
The firm must recover all $25,000 before printing
Printing adds $3,000 to profit relative to not printing, because the editing cost is sunk
Printing loses $22,000 because total cost is $37,000
PMC-COP-H-115.feedback: The current decision compares the $15,000 incremental revenue with the $12,000 avoidable printing cost.

PMC-COP-H-116.q: A fixed annual license can be surrendered halfway through the year for a $4,000 refund. For a midyear shutdown decision, which amount is relevant?
options: Only variable labor cost can be relevant
$0 because every fixed cost is sunk
The full original license price regardless of refund
PMC-COP-H-116.feedback: The recoverable amount differs across choices and is therefore avoidable rather than sunk.

PMC-COP-H-137.q: At Q = 1,000 the lowest ATC among three plants is $22; at Q = 2,000 it is $17; at Q = 3,000 it is $19. Which sequence best describes LRAC over these outputs?
options: It must equal the ATC of the smallest plant
PMC-COP-H-137.feedback: LRAC takes the lowest attainable ATC at each output, producing $22, $17, then $19.

PMC-COP-H-138.q: A firm increases every input by 50%, while output rises by 80%. Holding input prices constant, what should happen to average cost?
options: Average cost becomes fixed cost only
PMC-COP-H-138.feedback: Output rises more than proportionally to total input use, spreading cost over a larger proportional output increase.

PMC-COP-H-139.q: A manager blames rising LRAC at very large scale on “diminishing marginal product of labor.” What is the best correction?
options: Diseconomies require total product to fall
Diminishing marginal product and diseconomies are identical definitions
Diseconomies of scale are a long-run phenomenon involving changes in all inputs, not crowding one variable input against fixed inputs
The explanation is correct because the long run always has fixed capital
PMC-COP-H-139.feedback: Diminishing marginal product is a short-run concept; diseconomies concern scale when all inputs can vary.

PMC-COP-H-159.q: LRAC values are $22 at Q=1, $18 at Q=2, $15 at Q=3, $15 at Q=4, and $17 at Q=5. If quantities are thousands of units, which statement is correct?
options: MES is 5 thousand units because LRAC rises there
MES is 2 thousand units because LRAC is already falling
MES is 3 thousand units and constant returns hold from 3 to 4 thousand
MES is 4 thousand units because it is the largest minimum-cost output
PMC-COP-H-159.feedback: The minimum $15 first appears at 3 and remains unchanged through 4.

PMC-COP-H-160.q: A firm triples every input and output also triples. If input prices are unchanged, what happens to LRAC?
PMC-COP-H-160.feedback: Proportional output and input expansion implies constant returns to scale and unchanged long-run unit cost.

PMC-COP-H-161.q: A firm can produce 6,000 units at LRAC $20, 8,000 at $16, 10,000 at $16, and 12,000 at $18. What is the strongest conclusion?
options: MES is 8,000 units; 8,000–10,000 is a minimum-cost range
MES is 10,000 units because output is larger
MES is 12,000 units because LRAC turns upward there
There is no MES because two outputs share the minimum
PMC-COP-H-161.feedback: MES is the smallest output attaining the minimum $16 LRAC.

P62E-COP-EL-001.q: An owner reports $75,000 accounting profit but could earn $62,000 elsewhere and earn $18,000 renting owner capital. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Economic profit is −$5,000 even though accounting profit is positive
P62E-COP-EL-001.feedback: Subtract $80,000 of implicit costs from $75,000 accounting profit.

P62E-COP-EL-002.q: A firm’s economic profit is zero while its accounting profit rises because the owner’s outside salary falls by the same amount. Which statement is correct?
options: Normal profit is still being earned because total opportunity cost remains covered
P62E-COP-EL-002.feedback: The change in implicit cost offsets the accounting-profit change.

P62E-COP-EL-003.q: A restaurant can vary labor today but cannot expand kitchen space for six months. Six months is the relevant short run because:
options: Six months is legally defined as short run
Kitchen capacity remains fixed during that decision period
P62E-COP-EL-003.feedback: The fixed-input constraint defines the short run.

P62E-COP-EL-004.q: MP falls from 14 to 11 while remaining positive. What happens to TP?
options: TP rises by 11, but at a slower rate than before
P62E-COP-EL-004.feedback: Positive MP increases TP; the decline in MP slows the increase.

P62E-COP-EL-005.q: MP equals AP at 12 units per worker. The next worker has MP of 9. What happens to AP?
P62E-COP-EL-005.feedback: A marginal below the current average lowers the average.

P62E-COP-EL-006.q: A firm’s wage is constant. MP rises from 5 to 10 units per worker. What happens to MC attributable to labor?
P62E-COP-EL-006.feedback: MC=wage/MP in the simple one-variable-input model.

P62E-COP-EL-007.q: TFC rises by $1,000. At Q=100, which statement is exact?
options: All four per-unit curves rise by $10
AFC and ATC each rise by $10; AVC and MC do not change
AVC rises but ATC does not
P62E-COP-EL-007.feedback: The fixed-cost increase per unit is $1,000/100.

P62E-COP-EL-008.q: A per-unit royalty of $4 is added to production. Which immediate effect is correct?
options: AVC, ATC, and MC rise by $4 at every positive output
P62E-COP-EL-008.feedback: A constant per-unit cost adds $4 to variable and marginal cost.

P62E-COP-EL-009.q: At Q=50, AFC is $6 and AVC is $24. At Q=60, AFC is $5 and AVC is $23. Which statement is true?

P62E-COP-EL-010.q: MC rises from $18 to $22 while ATC falls from $30 to $28. Why is there no contradiction?
options: MC remains below ATC and therefore still pulls ATC down
P62E-COP-EL-010.feedback: The level of MC relative to ATC, not merely MC’s direction, controls ATC.

P62E-COP-EL-011.q: MC is $32 and ATC is $32 at Q=80. What can be inferred locally?
P62E-COP-EL-011.feedback: MC intersects ATC at minimum ATC.

P62E-COP-EL-012.q: MC intersects AVC before it intersects ATC in the standard graph. Why?
options: AVC reaches its minimum at a lower output than ATC
P62E-COP-EL-012.feedback: The averages have different minima because ATC includes falling AFC.

P62E-COP-EL-013.q: A firm’s fixed insurance premium is refundable if the plant closes. Which description is best?
options: Fixed in the current production range but not sunk
P62E-COP-EL-013.feedback: Fixed and sunk are different classifications.

P62E-COP-EL-014.q: A specialized mold has no resale value after purchase. For a current output decision, its purchase price is:
options: Sunk and irrelevant to marginal cost
P62E-COP-EL-014.feedback: The unrecoverable payment does not change with current output.

P62E-COP-EL-015.q: A new scheduling system reduces idle time without changing wages or plant rent. Which curves should fall?
options: AVC, ATC, and MC; AFC is unchanged
P62E-COP-EL-015.feedback: Higher labor productivity reduces variable and marginal cost.

P62E-COP-R-003.q: Accounting profit is $60,000 and implicit costs are $45,000. Economic profit?

P62E-COP-R-004.feedback: Zero economic profit means all opportunity costs are covered.

P62E-COP-R-005.q: Why can the short run last several years in one industry?

P62E-COP-R-006.q: In the short run, which statement must be true?

P62E-COP-R-017.feedback: A pure fixed-cost change leaves variable and marginal cost unchanged.

P62E-COP-R-018.q: The wage rises. Which curves shift upward?
P62E-COP-R-018.feedback: The wage is a variable-input price.

P62E-COP-R-019.q: Diminishing MP and diseconomies of scale differ because:

options: The smallest output attaining minimum LRATC

PMC-COP-R-010.q: A learner says, “If the owner did not write a check, the resource has no cost.

Every implicit cost must appear on an invoice
Opportunity cost matters only for consumers
Owner-supplied resources can have implicit opportunity costs even without a cash payment

PMC-COP-R-023.q: A learner subtracts the owner’s forgone salary when calculating accounting profit. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: The forgone salary should be added to revenue
Accounting profit subtracts explicit costs; the forgone salary is implicit
Accounting profit subtracts all opportunity costs
PMC-COP-R-023.feedback: Implicit costs matter for economic profit, not the accounting-profit calculation.

PMC-COP-R-024.q: A learner says economic profit equals accounting profit plus implicit costs. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: Economic profit and accounting profit are always equal
Economic profit equals accounting profit minus implicit costs
Economic profit equals accounting profit plus explicit costs
Economic profit ignores owner opportunity costs
PMC-COP-R-024.feedback: Implicit costs reduce economic profit relative to accounting profit.

PMC-COP-R-025.q: A learner calls zero economic profit a “loss.
options: Zero economic profit means all explicit and implicit costs, including normal profit, are covered
Zero economic profit means revenue is zero
Zero economic profit means explicit costs exceed revenue
Zero economic profit excludes owner compensation
PMC-COP-R-025.feedback: Normal profit is included in economic cost, so zero economic profit can be a sustainable outcome.

PMC-COP-R-026.q: A learner finds accounting profit of $50,000 and implicit cost of $70,000, then reports economic profit of $20,000. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: $20,000 is correct because profit cannot be negative

PMC-COP-R-043.q: A learner writes TC = TFC − TVC. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
PMC-COP-R-043.feedback: Total cost combines the fixed and variable components.

PMC-COP-R-044.q: A learner says fixed cost must fall when output falls. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: Fixed cost is another name for marginal cost
Within the short run, total fixed cost does not vary with output
Fixed cost moves one-for-one with output
Fixed cost equals zero below capacity
PMC-COP-R-044.feedback: A fixed input creates a cost that remains even as current output changes.

PMC-COP-R-045.q: A learner reports positive TVC when output is zero in the standard short-run schedule. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: At zero output, TVC is zero; any remaining cost is fixed
TVC equals TFC at zero output
TVC is always greater than TC
TVC is an implicit cost only
PMC-COP-R-045.feedback: Variable costs arise from producing output, while fixed costs remain at zero output.

PMC-COP-R-046.q: A row has TFC = $90 and TC = $250, but a learner records TVC = $340. Which statement best corrects this mistake?

PMC-COP-R-065.q: A learner divides output by TFC to calculate AFC. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
PMC-COP-R-065.feedback: Average fixed cost is fixed cost per unit of output.

PMC-COP-R-066.q: A learner calculates AVC using TC/Q. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
PMC-COP-R-066.feedback: TC/Q is ATC; AVC uses total variable cost only.

PMC-COP-R-067.q: A learner says ATC = AVC − AFC. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
PMC-COP-R-067.feedback: Average total cost contains both average variable and average fixed cost.

PMC-COP-R-068.q: A learner says AFC eventually rises because “all U-shaped costs rise.
options: AFC keeps falling as fixed cost is spread over more output
AFC equals MC at its minimum
PMC-COP-R-068.feedback: AFC is not U-shaped in the standard model; it declines as quantity increases.

PMC-COP-R-069.q: At Q = 10, AFC = $6 and AVC = $14. A learner reports ATC = $8. Which statement best corrects this mistake?

PMC-COP-R-089.q: A learner calculates MC as TC/Q. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
PMC-COP-R-089.feedback: TC/Q is average total cost; marginal cost uses changes.

PMC-COP-R-090.q: A learner says a higher fixed property tax must raise MC. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: Every fixed-cost increase raises MC one-for-one
MC equals AFC after a tax
Fixed costs are part of TVC
A pure fixed-cost increase does not change MC
PMC-COP-R-090.feedback: MC depends on changes in cost as output changes, and a fixed amount is present at every output.

PMC-COP-R-091.q: A learner says falling marginal product causes MC to fall. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: Marginal product and MC always move together
Marginal product affects fixed cost only
With a constant input price, falling marginal product raises MC
Falling marginal product lowers both MC and AVC automatically
PMC-COP-R-091.feedback: Less extra output from the same variable-input expense raises cost per additional unit.

PMC-COP-R-092.q: TC rises by $50 when output rises by 5 units, but a learner reports MC = $50. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
PMC-COP-R-092.feedback: Divide the cost change by the output change: $50/5 = $10.

PMC-COP-R-093.q: A worker costs $100 and adds 10 units. A learner reports MC from labor as $100 per unit. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: The labor cost per marginal unit is $10
The labor cost per marginal unit is $100
Marginal product should be added to the wage
The worker’s wage is a fixed cost
PMC-COP-R-093.feedback: Divide the worker’s cost by the worker’s marginal product: $100/10 = $10 per unit.

PMC-COP-R-102.q: A learner says MC must be falling whenever ATC is falling. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: ATC can fall only if MC is zero
MC and ATC always have the same slope
ATC falls only when AFC rises
MC can be rising while ATC is still falling, as long as MC remains below ATC
PMC-COP-R-102.feedback: The direction of the average depends on whether the marginal is above or below it, not on whether the marginal is itself rising.

PMC-COP-R-103.q: A learner says a higher fixed insurance premium shifts AVC and MC upward. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: All short-run curves shift by the same amount
A pure fixed-cost increase shifts AFC and ATC, not AVC or MC
A fixed-cost increase shifts only MC
PMC-COP-R-103.feedback: Fixed cost does not change the variable cost of current output or the incremental cost of another unit.

PMC-COP-R-117.q: A learner says, “Fixed cost and sunk cost mean the same thing.
options: A fixed cost can be avoidable in a future decision; a sunk cost is unrecoverable
Every sunk cost varies with output
Every fixed cost has already been paid forever
PMC-COP-R-117.feedback: Fixed describes how cost behaves with current output; sunk describes whether it can be recovered.

PMC-COP-R-118.q: A learner includes a nonrefundable past payment when comparing two current options that both leave the payment unchanged. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: Double the payment to reflect risk
Ignore the payment because it is sunk and identical across the options
PMC-COP-R-118.feedback: Only costs and benefits that differ across current alternatives should affect the choice.

PMC-COP-R-119.q: A learner calls a cancelable future lease payment sunk because the lease is a fixed cost. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: Only variable costs can be avoided
A lease payment is always implicit
The future payment is avoidable if canceling the lease eliminates it
PMC-COP-R-119.feedback: A cost can be fixed with respect to output yet avoidable with respect to a future decision.

PMC-COP-R-140.q: A learner treats LRAC as the ATC curve of one fixed plant. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: LRAC is total variable cost per unit only
LRAC reflects the lowest attainable ATC across alternative plant sizes
LRAC is the same as AFC
PMC-COP-R-140.feedback: The long run permits plant adjustment, so LRAC summarizes least-cost choices across plants.

PMC-COP-R-141.q: A learner says economies of scale mean total cost must fall as output rises. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: Economies of scale mean average cost falls; total cost can still rise
Economies mean fixed cost becomes zero
Economies require marginal product to be negative
PMC-COP-R-141.feedback: The concept concerns cost per unit, not necessarily the level of total cost.

PMC-COP-R-142.q: A learner says diseconomies of scale begin when marginal product first falls in the short run. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: Diseconomies and diminishing marginal product are the same event
Diseconomies require one input to remain fixed
Diseconomies concern long-run expansion of all inputs and rising LRAC
PMC-COP-R-142.feedback: The two concepts refer to different horizons and different input adjustments.

PMC-COP-R-143.q: A learner reads a downward-sloping LRAC segment as diseconomies of scale. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: LRAC slope says nothing about scale
A downward-sloping LRAC segment requires negative output
A downward-sloping LRAC segment represents economies of scale
A downward-sloping LRAC segment represents constant returns
PMC-COP-R-143.feedback: Falling long-run average cost as output expands is economies of scale.

PMC-COP-R-144.q: A learner says rising LRAC means output itself must be falling. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: Rising LRAC means total cost is falling
LRAC can rise while output expands; the issue is rising cost per unit at larger scale
Output and LRAC always move in opposite directions
PMC-COP-R-144.feedback: Diseconomies describe a higher average cost at greater output, not a fall in output.

PMC-COP-R-162.q: A learner chooses the largest output on a flat minimum-LRAC segment as MES. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: MES is always the largest efficient output
MES is where LRAC first begins to fall
MES is where total cost is smallest
MES is the smallest output that attains the minimum LRAC
PMC-COP-R-162.feedback: The definition focuses on the minimum scale required to achieve the lowest long-run unit cost.

PMC-COP-R-163.q: A learner says a flat LRAC means output is not changing. Which statement best corrects this mistake?
options: Flat LRAC means economies of scale
Flat LRAC means fixed cost is constant in the short run
Output can rise while LRAC stays constant; that range reflects constant returns to scale
Flat LRAC means output must be zero
PMC-COP-R-163.feedback: Constant returns refers to proportional changes in all inputs and output, leaving long-run cost per unit unchanged.

P62E-COP-BR-001.q: A proprietor uses a personally owned storefront. How does opportunity cost enter production cost?

P62E-COP-BR-004.q: Zero economic profit signals that owner resources earn:
P62E-COP-BR-004.feedback: Normal profit keeps owner resources in their current use.

P62E-COP-BR-005.q: A firm asks how much cost rises when output expands slightly. Which measure is relevant?
P62E-COP-BR-005.feedback: Marginal analysis focuses on incremental changes.

P62E-COP-BR-006.q: Why does MC below ATC lower ATC?

P62E-COP-BR-006.feedback: A below-average marginal observation pulls the average down.

P62E-COP-BR-007.q: A worker adds 10 units and costs $200. The labor-based MC is:
P62E-COP-BR-007.feedback: Divide the input cost by marginal product.

P62E-COP-BR-008.q: Which cost is irrelevant to the marginal cost of one more unit?

P62E-COP-BR-008.feedback: A cost that does not change has zero marginal contribution.

P62E-COP-BR-009.q: A productivity improvement raises output per worker. With wages unchanged, what happens to labor cost per unit?
P62E-COP-BR-009.feedback: More output from the same wage lowers unit cost.

P62E-COP-BR-010.q: A factory produces the same output with fewer labor hours. Which cost most directly falls?
P62E-COP-BR-010.feedback: Labor-hours savings lower current variable cost.

P62E-COP-BR-011.q: How can better organization create economies of scale?
options: Specialization and coordination may lower LRATC over an output range

P62E-COP-BR-012.q: For a competitive firm considering a change in output, which cost curve measures the incremental production cost?
P62E-COP-BR-012.feedback: Marginal cost measures the additional cost of producing more output and is the relevant cost measure for incremental output decisions.

P62E-COP-BR-013.q: Why does distinguishing AVC from ATC matter for a firm’s short-run production decisions?
options: The two averages contain different cost components
P62E-COP-BR-013.feedback: AVC excludes fixed cost; ATC includes it.

P62E-COP-BR-014.q: Cost curves can be reused across market structures because:

P62E-COP-BR-014.feedback: Revenue conditions differ, but cost construction follows production and input prices.

P62E-COP-BR-015.q: A higher wage paid for labor directly raises:

P62E-COP-BR-016.q: If the rental price of an adjustable machine service rises, what happens to cost?

P62E-COP-BR-016.feedback: An input-price increase raises production cost.

P62E-COP-BR-017.q: Why can a supply curve reflect marginal cost in a competitive setting?
